__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Select the Prometheus data source containing the PGX scrape jobs

title: PGX | vLLM Serving
description: Request rates, token throughput, TTFT, TPOT, latency and KV-cache pressure from job=pgx_vllm. Includes total, prompt, and generated token counts over the selected Grafana time range.

options.content:
**Source:** `pgx_vllm` · `pgx-vllm`  |  **What matters:** request latency, tokens/s, waiting work and KV cache.  Percentile charts require completed requests within the selected time window. **Companion:** use the dashboard link above to inspect DCGM GPUs + node exporter.

_vLLM v0/v1 cache and TPOT name fallbacks are included; other metrics follow current vLLM naming._

panels.title: KV cache utilization
panels.description: KV usage is a fraction internally. This panel converts it to percent; not the same as allocated VRAM.

panels.title: Requests completed / sec
panels.description: Count of completed requests; not all arrivals.

panels.title: Request concurrency & queue
panels.description: A rising queue with saturated concurrency indicates serving backpressure.

panels.title: Token throughput · prefill vs decode
panels.description: Counters converted to token rates. Model-level metrics may aggregate across engine processes.

panels.title: KV cache utilization (%)
panels.description: vLLM KV cache occupancy; distinct from CUDA/VRAM allocation reported by DCGM.

panels.title: 03 · Token usage · selected Grafana time range
Total tokens · selected range
panels.description: Prompt tokens processed + generation tokens produced during the currently selected Grafana time range. Uses increase() to adjust for vLLM counter resets. Limited to Prometheus data retention; this is not an all-time billing ledger.

panels.title: Prompt tokens · selected range
panels.description: Prompt/prefill tokens processed during the selected time range. Cache reuse can make this different from request-level billable prompt tokens.

panels.title: Generated tokens · selected range
panels.description: Output tokens produced during the selected time range.

panels.title: Time to first token · TTFT (ms)
panels.description: p50/p95/p99 of time from request submission to first streamed token.

panels.title: End-to-end request latency (seconds)
panels.description: End-to-end latency across completed requests, including generated output length.

panels.title: Time per output token · TPOT (ms)
panels.description: Per-request TPOT distribution, not instantaneous batch decode speed; fallback supports old metric name.

targets.expr: 1000 * (histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="pgx_vllm"}[$__rate_interval]))) or histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="pgx_vllm"}[$__rate_interval]))))

1000 * (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="pgx_vllm"}[$__rate_interval]))) or histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="pgx_vllm"}[$__rate_interval]))))

1000 * (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="pgx_vllm"}[$__rate_interval]))) or histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(vllm:time_per_output_token_seconds_bucket{job="pgx_vllm"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Request queue latency (ms)
panels.description: Time requests spend WAITING before processing starts.

panels.title: Completed requests / sec · finish reason
panels.description: Check the finish-reason distribution for truncation, aborts, errors or normal completions. Label values vary by release.

panels.title: Prefix cache token hit ratio (%)
panels.description: vLLM v1 prefix-cache token hit ratio. Empty on versions without these counters or when no queries exist.

panels.title: Average request size · tokens
panels.description: Mean prompt and generated tokens per completed request based on histogram sum/count.

panels.title: Preemptions / sec
panels.description: Frequent preemptions can indicate KV-cache pressure or scheduling contention. Common in v1.
